record.original_question: Derive incompleteness results for the determination of quantum algorithmic information.

evidence.quote: Derive incompleteness results for the determination of quantum algorithmic information. (K. Svozil)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let quantum algorithmic information theory denote any framework that assigns to a quantum object (e.g., a pure state |ψ⟩ on a finite- or countably-infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, a quantum circuit, or an infinite sequence of measurement outcomes) a notion of algorithmic information content C(|ψ⟩), generalizing classical Kolmogorov complexity. Concretely, fix a universal quantum description language: a universal quantum Turing machine (or equivalently a universal quantum circuit family) U, and define the quantum algorithmic information C_U(|ψ⟩) of a quantum state |ψ⟩ as the minimum length of a (classical) description of a quantum program that, when executed by U, outputs a state arbitrarily close to |ψ⟩ in trace distance.

Problem. Derive incompleteness theorems for the determination of quantum algorithmic information. Specifically, prove a result of the following form: for any recursively axiomatizable, sound formal system F that is sufficiently strong to formalize basic quantum mechanics and the definition of C_U, there exists a constant N_F such that for every quantum state |ψ⟩ (in some natural recursively enumerable family of finitely describable states) and every integer n > N_F, the system F cannot prove any statement of the form "C_U(|ψ⟩) > n", even when this statement is true for all but finitely many states. Equivalently, exhibit explicit limits on the provability of lower bounds for quantum algorithmic information, in analogy with Chaitin's incompleteness theorem for classical Kolmogorov complexity, and characterize the largest n for which F can prove such lower bounds.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem (posed by K. Svozil) appears to remain open as a general program. While classical Chaitin-style incompleteness for Kolmogorov complexity is well established, and recent work (e.g., consequences of MIP*=RE for operator algebras and Connes' Embedding Problem, and surveys on undecidability in physics) provides related undecidability/incompleteness phenomena in quantum information, no comprehensive analogue of Chaitin's incompleteness theorem specifically for quantum algorithmic information has been verified as established.

status_evidence.title: Undecidability and incompleteness in quantum information theory and operator algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys incompleteness results in operator algebras stemming from MIP*=RE, including a Gödelian refutation of the Connes Embedding Problem.
status_evidence.claim: Related incompleteness results in quantum information exist but address operator-algebraic problems rather than quantum Kolmogorov complexity directly.

status_evidence.title: Algorithmic Randomness, Quantum Physics, and Incompleteness
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses new faces of the incompleteness phenomenon via algorithmic information and quantum computing, citing Svozil's program.
status_evidence.claim: The intersection of quantum mechanics and algorithmic incompleteness is an active program, with Svozil's questions still being pursued.

status_evidence.title: Undecidability in Physics: a Review
status_evidence.snippet: Recent review of undecidability results across physics, including quantum information.
status_evidence.claim: A general incompleteness theorem specifically for quantum algorithmic information is not reported as established.
